title: Gyeran Jjim Steamed Eggs
shortDescription: Eggs are gently cooked with anchovy-kelp broth until softly set and steaming, then finished with scallion and sesame oil.
culturalContext: Gyeran jjim is a Korean steamed or gently simmered egg dish. Vessel, broth, toppings, and texture vary from silky home versions to puffed earthenware presentations.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Small heavy saucepan with lid or heat-safe earthenware pot

instructions.heading: Mix eggs and broth
instructions.action: Beat eggs with salt, then whisk in cool broth; strain if a finer texture is desired.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The mixture is uniform and lightly foamy.
instructions.safetyNote: Wash hands and clean spills after handling raw egg.

instructions.heading: Warm gently
instructions.action: Pour into the pot and cook over medium-low, stirring slowly along the bottom and sides.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Small soft curds begin to form.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not leave the pot unattended.

instructions.heading: Cover to set
instructions.action: Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook gently without a hard boil.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Edges are set and the center jiggles as one mass.
instructions.safetyNote: Open the lid away from your face to avoid steam burns.

instructions.heading: Verify temperature
instructions.action: Insert a clean thermometer into the center without touching the pot; continue cooking until 160°F / 71°C.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The center reaches 160°F / 71°C with no liquid egg.

instructions.heading: Finish
instructions.action: Remove from heat, top with scallion and sesame oil, and rest covered briefly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The surface is softly set and steaming.
instructions.safetyNote: The pot and escaping steam remain very hot.

instructions.heading: Serve promptly
instructions.action: Spoon into clean bowls and serve hot.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The custard is tender and steaming throughout.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this egg dish is gently cooked in a covered pot.
targetInternalTemperature: 160°F / 71°C in the center of the egg dish.
visualDonenessCues: Edges and center are softly set
foodSafetyNotes: Open the lid away from your face to avoid steam burns.
Refrigerate within 2 hours at or below 40°F / 4°C.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains egg, fish, and sesame; verify the broth and prevent cross-contact.

substitutions: Use water or a verified allergen-appropriate vegetable broth in place of anchovy-kelp broth.
ingredientSourcing: Verify prepared broth labels for fish and other allergens.
makeAhead: For best texture, mix just before cooking; broth may be prepared and refrigerated 1 day ahead.
storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours in a covered shallow container and use within 4 days pending food-safety approval.
reheating: Reheat gently until the center reaches 165°F / 74°C and is steaming.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers promptly; the texture will be firmer.
servingSuggestions: Serve immediately with rice and grilled foods.

faq.question: Why did the eggs turn rubbery?
faq.answer: The heat may have been too high or cooking too long; use gentle heat while still reaching 160°F / 71°C.

faq.question: Is gyeran jjim always made in earthenware?
faq.answer: No. Pots and cooking methods vary.
